Ternopil Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Ternopil's Jews were among the town's first settlers when it was founded in 1540, and by the early 19th century the city had become a center of the Haskalah in Galicia. Yosef Perl (1773–1839), one of the movement's leading figures, was born here, and other illustrious Maskilim who lived in the town included Nachman Krochmal (1785–1840) — born in Brody, documented elsewhere in this collection — Mendel Satanover (1749–1826), and S.L. Goldberg (1807–46). The Jewish population peaked at 13,842 (50.5 percent of the town) in 1890. A pogrom two days after the German occupation of July 1941 claimed thousands of lives; the ghetto's liquidation in June 1943 and the labor camp's closure that August together claimed around 3,000 more. This is the older of Ternopil's Jewish cemeteries, dating to around 1550 per IAJGS and POLIN Museum researchers, closed in the 1840s when a new cemetery opened, and finally demolished in the 1960s after being vandalized during WWII.
